note: The rendered check's rows and the sabotages that prove each one sees (#597, #807). Read by browser-checks/rendered_features.mjs, which runs the rows, and by browser-checks/lib/sabotage.py, which breaks a copy of the site one way at a time. Both platforms call the same two files, so the rows live here once. Deliberately NOT in contracts/: nothing here is a sentence a teacher reads or a rule the product follows; it is a test both platforms run (the #597 plan, section 4). The product rule that a site asks nothing of any other host becomes a contract with #566.

thirdPartyHostsToday.why: What a built site asks of other hosts on Quartz 4.5.0 (measured 2026-11-13 on every fixture page, both engines): the theme's Google Fonts stylesheet and its faces, and Mermaid's engine from cdnjs on a page with a diagram. #566 empties this list. A request to any other host fails the own-host row, so a NEW third party is red already.

expectedConsole.why: Netlify injects its ad badge into every page; the site's policy refuses its script inside an about:srcdoc frame, by design, 700 to 850 ms after first paint, in both engines (settled on #625; documentation/07, Suppressing Netlify's own ad badge).

engines.chromium: Chrome for Testing, the copy documentation/06 F7 installs (PLANTOIR_CHROME or --chrome), driven through Playwright's executablePath so it is the same binary as every other browser check.
engines.webkit: Playwright's WebKit build, the one playwright-core 1.63.0 pins (webkit-2359, WebKit 26.6 on this Mac), from browser-checks/fetch-browsers.sh's cache.

rows.name: mermaid
rows.passes: every code.mermaid ends with a drawn svg holding text, and again after the site's own dark-mode button is pressed

rows.name: katex
rows.passes: formulas set (.katex, no .katex-error) and, after document.fonts.load, a KaTeX_Main face whose status is loaded; never document.fonts.check(), which answers true for a family that does not exist and, in WebKit, for a face whose file failed

rows.name: tikz
rows.passes: the drawing's svg is on the page with a width and a height

rows.name: graph
rows.passes: a path.line whose d has more than one segment

rows.name: python
rows.passes: Run pressed for real prints 42; then a program that reads a line takes a typed World (live, in its answer field, where the host isolates the page; in its box otherwise) and prints Hello, World

rows.name: swift
rows.passes: Run pressed for real prints 42

rows.name: quiz
rows.passes: a wrong choice then the right one, each checked by a real press and answered in the contract's words (quizCallouts.words.site notRight, then right)

rows.name: tasks
rows.passes: a box ticked by a real press is still ticked after a reload

rows.name: progress
rows.passes: My Progress, opened after that tick, reads 1 / 2 on the Tasks page's row

rows.name: geogebra
rows.passes: the file sketch opens on a real press: its canvas, from the site's own engine

rows.name: geogebra drag
rows.passes: point A dragged with real pointer events moves (#755)

rows.name: geogebra reset
rows.passes: GeoGebra's reset icon, pressed for real where geogebraFences.reset.icon puts it, puts A back where the sketch opened it (#792)

rows.name: geogebra keys
rows.passes: Shift+Tab and Space pressed again and again while the 150-line sketch's lines run leave all 150 points, and a press on its reset icon brings back all 150 (#792 item 12)

rows.name: embeds
rows.passes: each YouTube, Vimeo, geogebra.org and PhET frame navigated to a document that answered 2xx (the frame's own response, never only a load event, which also fires on an error page). Deployed sites only: the embeds need the network and nothing in them is the site's

rows.name: pdf
rows.passes: the handout's PDF link answers 200 with application/pdf

rows.name: print
rows.passes: Print pressed for real and a way of printing chosen: the print layout laid out at least one page, the diagram drawn on it, and the handout's Latin Modern face loaded (judged by its FontFace status)

rows.name: copy
rows.passes: the text block's copy button, pressed by a real pointer at its centre, is what the pointer hits and writes the block's text (#759; WebKit is where it was found). Read through a spy on navigator.clipboard.writeText, since WebKit refuses readText and has no clipboard permission to grant

rows.name: heading anchor
rows.passes: loaded with #test-of-success under eight runnable blocks: once they and the page's height have settled, the window is moved 400 px by a script (as the sidebar's own scroll to its entry moves it, #604) and 1,500 px more arrive above the heading (as a late diagram, picture or editor does over a real network). On this Mac every piece arrives before the page is shown, and WebKit keeps a fragment in view by itself until a script scrolls, so without these nothing would move and the row would pass with the site's landing gone (measured 2026-11-13). Then the heading must be in the top third of the window. WebKit has no scroll anchoring of its own; Chromium's is switched off, the imitation heading_anchor.mjs has always used

rows.name: fonts
rows.passes: the first family of each of the theme's three font settings that is not one of the device's own has at least one face whose status is loaded (not every face: display=swap loads only the weights the text uses)

rows.name: clean page
rows.passes: no console error and no page error but the expected lines for the host, no request refused by a policy (Chromium: a blocked request; WebKit: its Refused to line), no mixed content

rows.name: own host
rows.passes: every request any frame or worker made, seen through the context's own router (WebKit hands a worker's requests to no page or context listener; #597 review H1), went to the site's host or to one of thirdPartyHostsToday

rows.name: cold visit
rows.passes: five cold visits to the isolated Python page, each in a new context: fails when two or more take over 3 s to first contentful paint or the median does; one slow sample earns one counted retry (#625; read from performance paint entries, never a screenshot, which stays blank in headless WebKit until load)

sabotages.name: progress manifest

sabotages.name: geogebra file
sabotages.does: the sketch's .ggb cut to half its length; the drag and the reset need that sketch open; the 150-line sketch is made from lines and must still pass

sabotages.name: geogebra dialog
sabotages.does: a script that removes one of GeoGebra's dialogs from the open file sketch the way the loader did before #755 (dialog and shade removed, never closed), which leaves the applet ignoring a pointer; the reset row drags first, so it is red too, and GeoGebra itself throws when its dialog is gone (measured: a page error in both engines), which the clean-page row must see

sabotages.name: geogebra keys
sabotages.does: a script that stops the loader holding back Space and Enter while a sketch's lines run, the state before #792 review M1
sabotages.whyNotEveryGate: Not run by --expect-red all, only by name: it does not turn the row red reliably. Measured 2026-11-13: with the hold dropped the presses do reset the construction while its lines run (Chromium: 0 to 3 of 150 objects through 400 presses), but the loader's other half of #792, the hidden marker that tells it a reset got in, then rebuilds all 150; WebKit was left with 114 of 150 once in four runs and all 150 in the other three, Chromium all 150 every time. A sabotage that only sometimes fails would fail the gate at random. The row's must-fail is geogebra_applet.mjs item 12's, against the first version of #792 (82 and 75 of 150, Chromium).

sabotages.does: the handout's PDF removed
